title: How does the Memorization of Neural Networks Impact Adversarial Robust Models?

problem.claim: The work studies how memorization affects adversarially trained neural networks.

gap.claim: Adversarially trained models can memorize atypical and adversarially perturbed atypical samples but still exhibit poor clean accuracy and robustness on test data.

contributions.claim: Memorizing atypical samples improves accuracy on clean atypical samples but provides little improvement in adversarial robustness, and memorizing certain atypical samples can harm performance on typical samples.
Benign Adversarial Training avoids fitting harmful atypical samples while fitting as many benign atypical samples as possible.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that BAT achieves a better clean-accuracy-versus-robustness trade-off than baseline methods on benchmark image-classification datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: Prior studies associate memorization of atypical samples with strong performance in overparameterized neural networks.
Adversarial training can also memorize atypical samples, yet adversarially trained models suffer from poor clean accuracy and robustness on test data.
Memorization helps clean atypical accuracy more than adversarial robustness and may damage performance on typical samples.
The authors propose BAT and report improved clean-accuracy-versus-robustness trade-offs on benchmark image-classification datasets.

source_observation.claim: Memorization of atypical samples may improve clean accuracy without substantially improving adversarial robustness.

interpretation.claim: Memorization should be evaluated separately for clean performance and robustness rather than treated as uniformly beneficial.

application.claim: When analyzing adversarial training, measure the effects of fitting atypical samples on both clean accuracy and adversarial robustness.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this pattern holds beyond the reported setting.

source_observation.claim: Certain atypical samples can harm performance on typical samples.

interpretation.claim: Selective avoidance of harmful atypical samples may be preferable to indiscriminate fitting.

application.claim: Training procedures can distinguish between atypical samples that are beneficial and those that impair typical-sample performance.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify how harmful and benign atypical samples are identified.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baseline methods, model architectures, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not explain how BAT identifies harmful versus benign atypical samples.
The abstract does not provide experimental protocols or robustness threat models.
